newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Yonhap says N.Korea doubles grain ration.
newsitem.headline: Yonhap says N.Korea doubles grain ration.

text.p: North Korea has recently doubled the grain ration for its hunger-hit people, but the relief is likely to only be temporary, South Korean media reported on Thursday.

Yonhap News Agency quoted a South Korean Foreign Ministry official as saying that a source recently returned from North Korea had reported the daily grain ration had been raised from 200 grams to 450 grams following this autumn's harvest.
"The official went on to say that the northern authorities would have to reduce the ration early next year as grain stocks began to run out," Yonhap said.

The South Korean official estimated North Korea needed an estimated five million tons of grain a year to meet the minimum needs of its population,but the harvests this year had brought in only 3.5 million tons.
North Korea has been hit for the past two years by heavy rain and floods that have caused widespread crop and other damage.

"We don't see any possibility of North Korea collapsing in the immediate future because of a food shortage. Malnutrition and disease, caused by a diet consisting only of corn and potatoes, will, however, lead to the eventual collapse of the North," Yonhap quoted the official as saying.
In Washington on Wednesday, United States Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) Director John Deutch painted an equally bleak picture of North Korea's future.
He said that within three years, North Korea would be at war with South Korea, would collapse as a state or be on the road to reunification.
"How that proceeds between those three directions will be resolved in the next two or three years. It is not something that will go on for decades," he said.
